title: 2016 Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations Il-76 crash
operator: Ministry of Emergency Situations of Russia

location.name: Near Lake Baikal, northeast of Irkutsk, Siberia

summary: An Ilyushin Il-76 aerial firefighting aircraft crashed near Lake Baikal while operating at minimum altitude over a wildfire area. The hot air from the wildfires reduced engine thrust, causing loss of altitude. The tail struck a hillock, then the aircraft collided with the hillside. All ten crew members were killed.
probable_cause: Loss of engine thrust caused by hot air from the wildfires resulted in loss of altitude; tail struck terrain leading to collision with hillside. (p. 11-13)

factors.evidence: Wildfires in Siberia created hot air conditions in the area (p. 11)
Hot air from wildfires caused loss of engine thrust, resulting in loss of altitude (p. 13)
SRPBZ warnings 'PULL UP' and 'TERRAIN AHEAD' registered repeatedly for 7 minutes (p. 12)
Aircraft tail struck hillock at 945m elevation, then collided with hillside (p. 13)

events.text: Aircraft departed for firefighting mission in Kachugsky District (p. 11)
Aircraft at 3,300m altitude on course 45 degrees, speed 450 km/h (p. 11)
Initial contact with dispatcher; reported ETA to work area 03:02 (p. 11)
Crew reported arrival at work area and beginning descent to 500-50m working altitude (p. 11-12)
SRPBZ warnings activated; terrain avoidance alerts PULL UP and TERRAIN AHEAD registered continuously (p. 12)
Commander decided on further descent; parameters speed 345 km/h heading 190 deg altitude 210m approaching target at 5km (p. 13)
At 55th minute of flight aircraft collided with hillside slope; broke apart and caught fire (p. 13)

recommendations.text: Disseminate information about this accident to flight and technical personnel operating Il-76 aircraft (p. 36)
Conduct additional training with aviation personnel on characteristics of firefighting operations (p. 36)
Study SRPBZ and EGPWS system operation and procedures for crew actions when ground proximity warnings activate (p. 36)

notes: Read history of flight (p. 11-13), operative recommendations (p. 36)
Intermediate report format; full conclusions pending
